anomaly_def.Name: MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly + Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly + Replication Synchronization Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
MVCC Version Maintenance Anomaly : Obsolete row versions, rollback records, and dead index entries accumulate faster than background cleanup can reclaim them, inflating storage, slowing visibility checks, and risking transaction-ID horizon exhaustion.
Database Configuration Parameter Anomaly : Memory, checkpoint, logging, parallelism, or worker-throttling parameters are mis-tuned relative to hardware and workload intensity, so internal subsystems are starved or overfed despite physical resources still being available.
Replication Synchronization Anomaly : Standbys or downstream consumers cannot receive, persist, or apply WAL/redo at the rate the primary emits it, causing widening replay lag and preventing log recycling.

When these three root causes coexist, the database experiences a compound failure pattern: the primary’s tables and indexes bloat rapidly with unreclaimed MVCC versions, inflating every sequential scan and index probe. Mis-sized memory pools and conservative autovacuum, checkpoint, or WAL retention parameters further slow cleanup and increase log generation, while low parallel-apply settings and network or I/O bottlenecks keep replicas perpetually behind. Operators observe runaway disk-space growth both in the main heap and in retained transaction logs, prolonged query latencies on the primary due to larger on-disk footprints and misestimated statistics, frequent checkpoint or flush storms that do not coincide with actual hardware utilization, and escalating replication lag that threatens recovery-point objectives and impedes failover. Monitoring shows autovacuum or equivalent cleaners saturated yet ineffective, while replica apply processes choke on the swollen stream of undo/redo generated by repeated table rewrites and bloated updates.

Causally, poor configuration choices (e.g., undersized autovacuum workers, small maintenance work memory, aggressive checkpoint completion targets, oversized per-session work_mem) hamper version cleanup and increase WAL churn. The resulting MVCC bloat amplifies redo volume and I/O pressure, which must traverse the replication pipeline. Because replicas are already lag-prone, additional log traffic pushes them further behind, forcing the primary to retain more logs and preventing space reclamation. The retained logs, in turn, keep old snapshots alive on replicas, extending the global xmin horizon and blocking vacuum from pruning dead tuples on the primary, which feeds back into even faster table growth. Thus, each anomaly reinforces the others: mis-tuned parameters throttle housekeeping, MVCC debris inflates both data and log streams, and replication lag prolongs version retention, collectively degrading OLTP performance and storage health far more severely than any single issue alone.

entry.official_definition: Controls how long STOP REPLICA waits before timing out.
entry.trigger_condition: A STOP REPLICA administrative operation waits longer than rpl_stop_replica_timeout.
entry.workload_impact: The administrative replication stop operation times out.
entry.default_behavior: Defined as a MySQL replication system variable.
entry.cause_analysis: This timeout is usually triggered when replication endpoints stop exchanging or applying data within the configured timeout window, causing the channel to be considered inactive.
entry.solution_guidance: Inspect replication channel health, sender/receiver status, upstream and downstream connectivity, and whether lag or stalled apply is preventing timely progress.
